newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Saudis see market strong enough to absorb Iraq oil.
newsitem.headline: Saudis see market strong enough to absorb Iraq oil.

text.p: OPEC linchpin Saudi Arabia believes that the world oil market is strong enough to absorb a resumption of Iraqi exports, a Gulf source said on Tuesday.
But this source said it remained to be seen how soon a United Nations accord to let Iraq make limited oil sales to help it buy food and medicine would, in fact, be implemented.
"The market is very healthy. Demand is strong. Stocks are low. And winter has just started," the Gulf source said.

The source also stressed the importance that the Saudis and their Gulf Arab allies, Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates, continued to attach to the production quota system operated by the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries.
The Gulf source gave the indications of the Saudis' views as OPEC oil ministers assembled in Vienna for a conference opening on Wednesday.
The meeting will consider the prospect that Iraq may soon export oil for the first time since it invaded Kuwait in 1990.
The Gulf source said OPEC needed to maintain its system of setting production quotas as this served as a "stabilising force" on the oil market.
"The quota system is really very important. You need an organisation to serve as a stabiliser. Oil is a long term investment and a very risky commodity," the source said.

The comments by the source suggested that the Saudis with Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates probably felt that OPEC should maintain its present set of quotas at least through the first six months of next year.
The source said OPEC had when it last met back in June already dealt with the possible resumption of Iraqi exports when it gave Iraq an increased nominal quota of 1.2 million barrels per day (bpd).
"We gave them a quota already but you can't believe it (Iraq's return to the market) until you see it," the Gulf source said.

Although OPEC has a quota ceiling under the June agreement set at 25.03 million bpd, independent observers say it is already producing about 26 million, even without Iraq, because of quota violations.

But the comments by the Gulf course suggested that Saudi Arabia believes that oil demand is nonetheless able to absorb extra oil because of unusually low consumer stocks ahead of what so far looks like being a hard northern winter.
The Gulf source said that "demand is whatever OPEC is producing. We will definitely end this year with the lowest (industry) stocks in 20 years".
The source said demand for OPEC oil was at present clearly in excess of 26 million bpd.
